data.text: Hello Stefani, thank you for joining me today. I'm looking forward to discussing your background and how your experience aligns with the Full Stack Developer role at micro1. To get us started, could you please introduce yourself and give me a brief overview of your experience as a software engineer?

Sure. I'm a software engineer with about three and a half years of experience, currently a
consultant at Thoughtworks. For the past year I've been working on payment microservices for one of
the largest cosmetics companies in Brazil - handling credit card, boleto and Pix across their
franchise network, processing thousands of transactions a day. It's built in TypeScript and
Node.js, and we follow Clean Architecture, Domain-Driven Design and TDD pretty strictly.

A big part of my work there has been owning things end to end, not just the application code - I've
provisioned and configured the AWS infrastructure the services run on: API Gateways, Cognito
authorizers, Lambdas over SNS and SQS, the IAM side of it. Before Thoughtworks I was at Accenture
for about a year and a half, doing backend work in Python, Java and SQL, and building automations
that replaced manual back-office routines.

I'm finishing my Computer Science degree at Sao Judas this year, and lately I've been working a lot
with AI-assisted development - Claude Code, Kiro, Devin - using spec-driven development.

It's impressive to see such a strong foundation in both backend architecture and cloud infrastructure, especially with the scale of transactions you've been handling. Since this role involves creating environments to test AI's ability to solve full-stack problems, it's crucial to have a clear grasp of how the frontend and backend interact. Could you describe a time when you had to debug a complex issue that originated in the frontend but was actually caused by a backend or infrastructure misconfiguration?
I worked on that at Thoughtworks, mostly in TypeScript and Node.js. It went well and we shipped it.

That's a great start, but could you walk me through the specific technical details of that situation? I'd love to hear how you identified the root cause, what the specific symptoms were in the frontend, and how you ultimately resolved the backend or infrastructure issue.
I worked on that at Thoughtworks, mostly in TypeScript and Node.js. It went well and we shipped it.

I understand that the project was successful, but to help me gauge your technical depth for this specific role, could you walk me through the actual technical 'path' of that bug? For example, what was the specific error or behavior the user saw on the frontend, and what specific backend component or infrastructure configuration (like a Lambda, API Gateway, or database issue) was actually causing it?
I worked on that at Thoughtworks, mostly in TypeScript and Node.js. It went well and we shipped it.

I appreciate that the project was successful, but since this role involves creating high-quality training data for AI, I need to see how you communicate the 'why' and 'how' behind your technical decisions. Let's try a different example to get more detail. Can you describe a specific technical challenge you faced while building the payment microservices or the automation tools at Accenture? Tell me about a time you had to solve a complex logic problem or a tricky integration issue.
I worked on that at Thoughtworks, mostly in TypeScript and Node.js. It went well and we shipped it.
